ServerJob.description:
Which workflow job produced a row.

Ours to name, so it is a closed set. Every other identifier on a host row is
a string the machine chose and cannot be one - see
`docs/reference/host-metrics.md`. Refusing anything else is what stops a typo
becoming a job nobody can group by.

Every value is a job's own id in its workflow file, lowercase, so a reader
goes from a row to the steps that wrote it with no lookup table in between.
A display name would drift from the thing it identifies.

**`visuals` is here for the rows and not for a job.** `digest.yml` ran one
until 2026-09-13, when the small model, its job and its flag were retired
together. Six committed counters rows still carry the value, and a member
with no producer left is the only thing that can read them back.
ServerJob.title: ServerJob

changelog.why: A job's clock is only known at its end, so the row arrives in two halves.

changelog.change: Widened `job` to every workflow job that draws its own machine.
changelog.why: A run whose slowest job is unmeasured is a run whose cost nobody can attribute.

changelog.change: Initial shape: the silicon a job drew, its instruction set and its bandwidth.
changelog.why: Throughput moved 3.7x by machine and nothing recorded which machine.

description: One job, one machine, one row: what the host said it was.

boot_seconds.description: How long the machine had been up when the job reached this probe. A small number is a freshly started virtual machine; a large one is a pooled machine this job was handed.
boot_seconds.title: Boot Seconds

cores.description: Physical cores the job can see.
cores.title: Cores

cpu_family.description: `cpu family`. With model and stepping this names the part.
cpu_family.title: Cpu Family

cpu_model.description: The `model name` line, in the host's own words.
cpu_model.title: Cpu Model

cpu_model_number.description: `model`, the number rather than the marketing name.
cpu_model_number.title: Cpu Model Number

fingerprint.description: A digest over the columns that cannot change inside a job - vendor, family, model, stepping, core counts, cache and flags. Two jobs on the same kind of machine carry the same value, which is what makes a distribution countable without matching model-name strings by hand. Absent on the half a job writes at its end, which carries the clock and repeats nothing the probe already recorded.
fingerprint.title: Fingerprint

flags.description: The watched instruction-set flags this host reported, sorted and space joined. Empty means none of them, which is itself a reading.
flags.title: Flags

job.description: The workflow job that drew this machine. Every job that draws its own runner writes one row, because a run is only as fast as its slowest job.

job_seconds.description: The job's own wall clock. The truncation cap reverts on the slowest work job's, and before this cell the only place that number lived was the GitHub jobs API, which drops a job record when the run ages out.
job_seconds.title: Job Seconds

l3_cache_bytes.description: L3 as the host reports it. Read beside `memcpy_probe_mib`: a probe buffer smaller than this measured cache rather than memory.
l3_cache_bytes.title: L3 Cache Bytes

measured_at.description: When the probe read this machine. Absent on the half a job writes at its end, which measured no machine.
measured_at.title: Measured At

memcpy_gib_s.description: Large-block copy bandwidth, bytes read plus bytes written, the way STREAM counts a copy. Decode is bandwidth bound and nothing else here measures bandwidth. Absent where the probe was switched off.
memcpy_gib_s.title: Memcpy Gib S

memcpy_probe_mib.description: The buffer each side of the copy used. Below `l3_cache_bytes` the figure is a cache reading.
memcpy_probe_mib.title: Memcpy Probe Mib

mhz_at_probe.description: The mean `cpu MHz` across processors at the moment of the probe. Not a reading under load - the probe runs before the model server starts - so it says what the machine idles at, never what it sustains.
mhz_at_probe.title: Mhz At Probe

mhz_max.description: `CPU max MHz`, where the host publishes one.
mhz_max.title: Mhz Max

microcode.description: `microcode` revision, which moves under a fixed stepping.
microcode.title: Microcode

model_load_ms.description: Milliseconds the server spent opening the weights before the first item. Once per job, which is this row's grain.
model_load_ms.title: Model Load Ms

runner_name.description: The runner label the platform gave this job.
runner_name.title: Runner Name

shard.description: The shard within that job. A single-shard job writes 0.
shard.title: Shard

threads.description: Logical processors. Four on every stock runner so far.
threads.title: Threads

vm_fault_domain.description: The fault domain, which separates one rack from another.
vm_fault_domain.title: Vm Fault Domain

vm_location.description: The region the metadata service named.
vm_location.title: Vm Location

vm_size.description: The platform's own name for this machine size, from the host metadata service. This is the placement decision in the platform's vocabulary rather than ours. Absent where the service did not answer.
vm_size.title: Vm Size

vm_zone.description: The availability zone, where the platform publishes one.
vm_zone.title: Vm Zone
